clue.text: For example, this party game

parts.note: the words being read are themselves an example of a clue, so they stand for the word CLUE
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone offers up a party game as an example of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example, this' points at the clue itself: this sentence is one example of a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluedo is a classic board game of murder detection, played as a parlour or party game.

clue.text: Singing test taken by small child

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for child
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A small child sits a singing exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' puts the child before the test in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music sung by a choir, so it is an adjective for vocal performance.

clue.text: Arthur's at sea crossing English Channel

indicators.note: crossing means the muddled letters go across, so around, the next piece
at sea means confused, so the letters of the name are muddled

explanation.surface: Arthur is out on the water crossing the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English Channel' reads as one name; 'English' gives E and 'Channel' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The urethra is the duct that carries urine out of the body, an anatomical channel.

clue.text: Daughter's joining a corporation in fact

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A daughter really is joining a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is the old humorous word for a large stomach, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, one item of data.

clue.text: Work that involved colour spectra originally

definitions.text: Work that involved colour spectra originally

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical or literary work

indicators.note: originally tells us to take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A description of a famous scientific book that dealt with the colours of the spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Newton's book Opticks, whose experiments split white light into colour spectra.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton's treatise on light, titled Opticks, studied how white light splits into a spectrum of colours.

clue.text: Ginger and I consume Argentine meat product

indicators.note: consume means the earlier pieces swallow the next one

parts.note: to ginger up is to add pep
Juan Perón was the president of Argentina

explanation.surface: Ginger and I eat some Argentine meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' is not a person but liveliness, as in to ginger up. Juan Perón was the Argentine president.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried sausage, a cured pork and beef product.

clue.text: Cake decorator, hosting social gathering, serves fresh drink

indicators.note: hosting means the decorator word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: an icer is someone who ices cakes
a bee is a gathering for work and socialising, like a sewing bee

explanation.surface: A cake decorator holds a party and pours drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee is a community get-together, as in a spelling bee or quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice beer is a lager brewed by partly freezing it, served chilled as a refreshing drink.

clue.text: Told to go collecting money for deposit

indicators.note: collecting means the first piece gathers the next inside it

parts.note: someone told to go has been sent away
a dime is a US coin, a sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone is ordered off to collect cash for a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' suggests a payment; it is the matter left at the bottom of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles out of a liquid, a geological or chemical deposit.

clue.text: Humble in more ways than one

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something, the first of the ways
ST, street, is another kind of way, the second one

explanation.surface: Someone is described as being unassuming in every respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in more ways than one' tells you to find two different ways: a manner of doing (MODE) and a road (ST, street).
explanation.definitionFit: Unassuming and self-effacing people are humble, not given to boasting.

clue.text: Fools designed shapes to cover poster

indicators.note: to cover means the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
designed means the letters of shapes are arranged into a new pattern

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a poster

explanation.surface: Idiots have produced shapes to hide a poster on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the letters to SAPHES, and 'to cover' places the poster's two letters between its E and its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A saphead is an old informal word for a stupid person, a simpleton.

clue.text: Attempt to intimidate wild bears scoundrel let loose

indicators.note: wild means the letters of bears run out of order

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or traitor

indicators.note: let loose means the letters of let are freed into another order

explanation.surface: Wild bears and a villain are set free to scare people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns BEARS into SABRE, and 'loose' turns LET into TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle one's sabre is to threaten military force, a show of aggression to cow others.

clue.text: It's easy to understand in short story circles

indicators.note: circles means the story word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

indicators.note: short means the phrase for in loses its last letter

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Something is easy to understand in the world of short story writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like 'briefly'; it is IN = AT HOME, docked by 'short' to AT HOM, which FABLE 'circles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whose depths can be plumbed and comprehended is easy to grasp.

clue.text: Award prize, ignoring judge

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter for judge is left out

parts.note: a jemmy is a crowbar used to prize or lever something open

explanation.surface: Someone hands out a prize without any judge being consulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' is not a reward here but the verb or tool for levering open: a JEMMY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's annual award, a statuette.

clue.text: A girl unloved, treated like a locust

indicators.note: treated means the letters are processed, like a material, into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An unloved girl is treated like a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Locust swarms consume every plant in their path, so they are a byword for eating everything.

clue.text: Nobleman accompanies girl soldiers to see civic official

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman
May is a girl's name
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A lord escorts a girl and some troops to visit a town dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a city corporation in Britain, such as London's, holds this ceremonial office.

clue.text: Buckle my sandal, Casanova

indicators.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so the letters are bent into another order

explanation.surface: An instruction to a famous seducer to do up a sandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckle' looks like fastening a shoe; it means crumple.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was a notorious seducer, so his name stands for a womaniser.

clue.text: Peter has a rest prior to bank robbery

indicators.note: prior to means the earlier pieces come before the next one

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a break is a rest
ING is a Dutch banking group

explanation.surface: A man called Peter takes a break before robbing a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name; in thieves' slang it is a safe. 'bank robbery' looks like one phrase, but 'bank' gives ING, the Dutch bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking open safes to steal their contents is a specific kind of burglary or theft.

clue.text: European male student working in pursuit of college grade

indicators.note: in pursuit of means the following pieces come after the college letter

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
L is a learner, a student driver
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A European man is studying hard to get a college grade.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or rank within an organisation, a step in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Private entrance to see the girl in French ballet

parts.note: a GI is a private soldier in the US army

indicators.note: entrance to means the opening letter of the word see

parts.note: elle is French for she, the girl

explanation.surface: A soldier's way in to watch a girl dancing in a French ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French ballet' reads as one phrase; 'in French' goes with 'the girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giselle is a famous romantic ballet by Adolphe Adam, first staged in Paris in 1841.

clue.text: Fish recipe for sportsperson

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish like a ray
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe meaning take

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction for fish, served to an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who competes on ice or wheels in skating is an athlete in that sport.

clue.text: The legend of Jeremy Thorpe

indicators.note: of means the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A reference to the story of the Liberal politician Jeremy Thorpe.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Thorpe was a British Liberal Party leader in the 1970s whose career ended in scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story, a synonym for a fable or fiction.

clue.text: Thomas Kray with blow up doll

indicators.note: blow up means the letters are exploded and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Thomas Kray turns up with an inflatable doll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow up doll' reads as a single phrase, but 'blow up' is the anagram signal and 'doll' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A matryoshka is a Russian nesting doll, wooden figures that fit one inside another.

clue.text: Loyal Tatars protecting port

indicators.note: protecting means the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Faithful Tatars defend a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a Black Sea resort town in Crimea, site of the 1945 Allied conference.

clue.text: Host gains trick after discarding clubs in hand

indicators.note: gains means the shortened word takes the next piece inside it
after discarding means the host word first loses a letter

parts.note: an emcee is a master of ceremonies, a host
C is the card abbreviation for clubs
a ploy is a trick or ruse

explanation.surface: A card game: the host wins a trick after throwing away a club from their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after discarding' leaves EMEE, which 'gains' the trick in its middle. 'hand' looks like cards but means a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a worker, as in farmhand or factory hand: someone on the payroll.

clue.text: Novel Kinks song about sex

indicators.note: about means the song title goes round the next piece

parts.note: Lola is a 1970 hit by the Kinks
it is a common slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A new song by the Kinks deals with sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the noun, Nabokov's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is the 1955 book by Vladimir Nabokov, a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Tracey initially hurried on over to display her work, some say

indicators.note: over means the pieces so far are turned round to read the other way
initially means take the opening letter of the name

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: The artist Tracey rushed over to show off her latest piece, which critics dismiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole string round. Tracey Emin is the British artist whose unmade bed some critics refused to call art.
explanation.definitionFit: Detractors of conceptual artists dismiss their pieces as not being art at all.

clue.text: Paella, for instance, always has cheese?

parts.note: a paella is the shallow pan the Spanish dish is cooked in, so it is an example of a pan
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A question about whether paella always includes cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The dish takes its name from the paella pan it is cooked in.
explanation.definitionFit: Paneer is a fresh, unaged South Asian cheese often used in curries.
